t.zh: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref>弄清了三个数的顺序，还没问它们的大小。电路算出的值可以落在 [0, 1] 之外，屏幕却只显示得出 0 到 1，超出的部分画成最黑或最白。文件里的像素又常存成<wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>：0 到 255 的整数，255 最亮。
t.en: <level-ref to="1C1"></level-ref> settled the order of the three numbers but not their size. A circuit may compute values outside [0, 1], while a screen shows only 0 to 1 and draws whatever lies beyond as the darkest or the brightest. And files often store pixels as <wiki-ref to="uint8"></wiki-ref>: whole numbers from 0 to 255, 255 the brightest.

t.zh: 这一关的问题是：两个像素看上去一样白，存着的数一样吗？第一个任务对照每格存着的数，填出它显示出来的值；第二个任务把 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 像素写成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。每格的数都对才算对。
t.en: This level asks: when two pixels look equally white, do they hold the same number? The first task has you fill in each cell's displayed value from its stored one; the second, write uint8 pixels read by OpenCV as (R, G, B) in [0, 1]. It is right when every cell's numbers are.

after.zh: 像素值有<wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref>和类型：显示时截到两端，存着的数不变；处理时常把 uint8 换成 [0, 1] 的浮点数。
after.en: Pixel values have a <wiki-ref to="value-range"></wiki-ref> and a type: the display clips to the ends while the stored numbers stay; processing often turns uint8 into floats in [0, 1].

brief.zh: 对照每格存着的数，填出它在屏幕上显示出来的值。
brief.en: From each cell's stored number, fill in the value the screen displays.

hint.zh: 看画面里最白的几格：它们存的数都一样吗？
hint.en: Look at the whitest cells of the picture: do they all hold the same number?

why.zh: 这是存着的数，不是显示出来的：屏幕只显示得出 0 到 1，−0.2 画成 0，1.2 画成 1，而存着的数照旧不变。
why.en: These are the stored numbers, not the displayed ones: a screen shows only 0 to 1, so −0.2 is drawn as 0 and 1.2 as 1, while the stored numbers stay as they were.

brief.zh: 这两个像素是 OpenCV 读进来的 uint8 值：写成 [0, 1] 里的 (R, G, B)。
brief.en: These two pixels are uint8 values read by OpenCV: write them as (R, G, B) in [0, 1].

hint.zh: OpenCV 读进来的三个数按什么顺序排？
hint.en: In what order does OpenCV store the three numbers?

why.zh: 除以 255 没错，顺序却照 RGB 读了：OpenCV 读进来的三个数是 B、G、R，第一个数是蓝。
why.en: Dividing by 255 is right, but the numbers were read as RGB: OpenCV stores B, G, R, so the first number is blue.
